outcome: obstetric outcomes (second stage of labor duration, vacuum extraction rate, cesarean delivery rate, perineal laceration)
neonatal outcomes (adverse neonatal outcome, Apgar scores <7 at 5 min, arterial pH <7.1, neonatal intensive care unit admissions)
cohort: The study included all women with singleton pregnancies who attempted vaginal delivery at >=37 weeks and had no previous cesarean delivery, observed from 2013 to 2021.
finding: The study found no increased risk of obstetrical or neonatal complications during labor for individuals diagnosed with symphysiolysis during pregnancy.
mod_finding: No significant differences were observed in the rates of vacuum extraction, cesarean delivery, or perineal laceration between women with and without symphysiolysis.
